title: Mirabel and the Debt
premise: Elodie Reyes, a disgraced intelligence analyst fired from three agencies, receives a call on a burner phone that shouldn't exist — the voice belongs to Marcus Vane, his former mentor, presumed dead for two years. Vane claims a catastrophic infrastructure failure is being engineered to look like an accident, orchestrated by the same shadowy network that ruined Elodie's career. As Elodie follows Vane's cryptic breadcrumbs through ledgers, safehouses, and a family inheritance tied to the conspirators, he discovers the 'attack' is actually an elaborate cover for laundering a fortune — and that Vane may be its architect, not its enemy. In the end, Elodie must choose between exposing Vane and letting justice outside the law run its course, ultimately leaking the truth publicly while allowing Vane to vanish, keeping both his conscience and his belonging intact.
about_author: Hazel Galloway is the pen name of a former financial-crimes investigator who spent a decade inside compliance departments before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people trapped between institutions and their own consciences.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Three years after his dismissal, scraping by as a freelance auditor, Elodie receives a burner phone in the mail with no return address. When it rings, Marcus Vane's voice — dead two years — gives him forty-eight hours and one address. The emotional beat is disorientation curdling into dread: someone wants him back in the game.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the address he finds a storage unit containing falsified inspection reports for the Calder Viaduct, dated next month. Cross-referencing them, he recognizes the signature style of Halcyon Group — the firm whose paperwork got him fired. The beat is vindication tinged with paranoia: the conspiracy that ended his career never stopped.

chapters.title: What the Dead Mentor Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Vane, alive and hiding, watches Elodie from across a train platform, narrating why he faked his death — he found the same ledger and chose disappearing over dying. The chapters interleave as Vane leaves a second clue. The beat is grief reframed: the mentor Elodie mourned was running from the same wolf.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Following a paper trail, Elodie learns his late mother's estate shares a trustee with Halcyon: Aldous Merrick, a philanthropist whose foundation funnels money through the viaduct's maintenance contracts. His inheritance — modest, sentimental — is entangled in the scheme. The beat is violation: even his family memory has been weaponized.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Three Warnings
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Desperate for allies, he approaches a former colleague at the transport authority, Dana Okafor, who confirms the inspection anomalies but warns him off — two other analysts who flagged Halcyon lost everything. Flashbacks reveal each of his three firings was engineered. The beat is isolation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Accident Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane infiltrates a Halcyon logistics depot and discovers not sabotage plans but a rehearsal: sensors, timing drills, a controlled structural failure scheduled for the viaduct's centenary ceremony — with dignitaries present. He realizes the 'accident' will kill witnesses who know too much, including possibly Elodie. The beat is horror at scale.

chapters.title: Merrick's Table
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Using his inheritance claim as cover, Elodie gets a meeting with Merrick, who offers him reinstatement, money, and erasure of his record — if he returns the burner phone and forgets the ledger. Elodie realizes they know exactly where he stands. The beat is temptation met with cold clarity: the offer is a leash.

chapters.title: Burned Bridge, Burning City
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Refusing Merrick, Elodie goes dark; Dana tips off Halcyon under pressure, forcing Elodie into Vane's orbit for real. Together in a safehouse they assemble the full picture: the collapse launders a decade of embezzlement by destroying the physical evidence. The beat is wary partnership becoming trust.

chapters.title: Centenary
chapters.summary: Dual POV, climax. On ceremony day, Elodie and Vane split: Vane triggers the depot's own failsafe to jam the demolition charges while Elodie confronts Merrick on the viaduct itself, recording his confession as the crowd evacuates on a staged gas leak. A Halcyon operative nearly kills them; Dana, arriving unexpectedly, saves Elodie. The beat is terror transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: Mirabel
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, resolution. Named for his mother's village church bell that rang debts forgiven, the chapter shows the aftermath: the leaked recordings dismantle Halcyon; Merrick is arrested; Elodie, unemployable by choice, publishes independently. Vane disappears again, leaving a second burner phone — silent, but there. The beat is earned peace: belonging found outside every institution that failed him.
